business.inbound.noteCopy: Your copy of the consignment note, kept for you as it was signed. The carriage price is on it only where the agreed term makes the carriage yours to pay.
business.inbound.noteGone: The note could not be opened just now. Try again.
business.inbound.abroad.atBorderAt: At the border post at {where} since {when}
business.inbound.abroad.underBond: In the country under bond: not cleared in yet
business.inbound.abroad.yoursToClear: Under {term}, clearing it in is yours
business.inbound.abroad.supplierClears: Under {term}, your supplier clears it in
business.people.title: People
business.people.lede: Everyone signs in with their own phone and PIN. Whatever they do is recorded under their name.
business.people.invitedSub: Phone ending {ends} · added by {who} on {when} · joins when they sign in and say yes
business.people.invited: {name} is invited. They join when they sign in to the Business app with their own phone and say yes.
business.people.removed: {name} is out of the business. It takes effect on their next click.
business.people.addLede: By the phone number they sign in with. Nothing opens for them until they sign in with their own phone and PIN and say yes.
business.people.name: Their name
business.people.nameHint: How they appear here, and the name on what they do.
business.people.ownerAdds: An owner of the business adds and removes people.
business.people.lastOwner: You are the only owner. Make somebody else an owner before you leave or change your own role — a business always has one.
business.details.title: Business details
business.details.lede: What the business says about itself, how people reach it, and the places it uses.
business.details.recheck: The name and the registration number are what SeeBuyGet checked. Change either and the business goes back to not checked until you ask again.
business.details.placesLede: Ports, yards and addresses you have saved. Each one is yours alone — except the loading hours and bays you give a place of your own, which the carriers whose plans collect there read.
business.places.noLoading: Loading: any hour, any number of trucks
business.places.loadingHint: When goods can be loaded here, and how many trucks at once. Your carriers plan their trucks to it. Each carrier counts the bays for its own trucks only: it does not know the others loading here.
business.places.anyHour: Loaded at any hour. Tick to set the hours: a truck that comes before you open waits, and nothing is collected on a closed day.
business.system.title: Your system
business.system.lede: Your own system can be told each step of your loads, as this app shows them: {events}. Nothing about money. Each message is signed with your secret, tried for about two days, and listed here with what became of it.
business.system.none: No address yet: nothing is sent.
business.system.secretOnce: Your signing secret. Copy it now: it is not shown again.
business.system.addressHint: Starting with https://. Leave it empty to stop the messages.
business.system.ownerOnly: An owner gives the address and the secret. Anybody who may act sends a message again.
business.system.notArrived: It did not arrive yet. It is tried again by itself
business.system.nothingYet: Nothing sent yet. The next step of one of your loads is.
business.loads.coldChainBroken: Broken: {temp} °C read {when}, outside the {min}–{max} °C it must be kept in
business.loads.coldChainLate: Read with no signal; it reached us {when}, so it may be different now.
business.system.event.parcelHandedIn: A parcel handed in at the shop
business.system.event.parcelDisputed: A problem reported with a parcel
business.system.event.parcelDelayed: A parcel that will be late
business.system.msg.retrying: Not arrived yet: tried {count, plural, one {once} other {# times}}, tried again by itself {next}.
business.system.msg.gaveUp: Not arrived: given up after {count, plural, one {one try} other {# tries}}. Put your system right, then send it again.
business.keys.title: Keys for your own systems
business.keys.lede: With a key, your own system — your ERP, your warehouse system — can read your loads, post a load, write the seals on it before pickup, and withdraw one nobody has taken yet; and send parcels, paid from your parcel balance at the price shown, and call one off. All through the same checks as this app. A test key runs every check, prices a parcel, and keeps nothing. Never what a person must decide: a price to agree, paying money in, or who is in the business.
business.keys.ownerOnly: An owner makes keys and takes them away; each is recorded under their name.
business.keys.label: What it is for
business.keys.labelHint: The system that will hold it, such as "ERP".
business.keys.secretOnce: The key. Copy it into your system now: it is not shown again.
business.keys.revokeWarn: The next call your system makes with it is refused.
business.gln.label: Global Location Number
business.gln.lede: Your GLN, from GS1, names your company on the consignment notes and package labels of your loads. A receiving dock reads it to know the goods are yours.
business.gln.removed: GLN removed. Loads already posted keep the one they had.
business.clients.gln.lede: The GLN of {name}, from GS1: it names them as the sender on the notes and labels of the loads you send for them.
business.places.gln.hint: The place’s own GLN: yours for your own places, the port’s or the yard’s for theirs. Goods sent here carry it as the ship-to barcode on their labels.
business.papers.gsin: The whole shipment’s GSIN, on every label and on the consignment note: {gsin}. Give it to customs as the shipment’s reference.
business.papers.shipTo: Each label also carries the ship-to GLN {gln} as a barcode.
business.gs1.title: GS1 barcodes on your packages
business.gs1.lede: With a GS1 company prefix, each package of a load you post gets its own SSCC, printed as a GS1-128 barcode beside our code: what a receiving warehouse scans into its own system. Without one, your labels carry our code alone.
business.gs1.none: No GS1 company prefix: your labels carry our code alone.
business.gs1.prefixHint: As GS1 gave it to you: 6 to 12 digits. We never make one up.
business.gs1.digitHint: One your own systems do not use, so a code is never given twice.
business.gs1.removed: No more GS1 codes. Loads keep the ones they have.
business.gs1.badPrefix: A GS1 company prefix is 6 to 12 digits.
business.gs1.ownerOnly: An owner of the business sets this.
business.gs1.claimLedeClient: Send SeeBuyGet staff {name}’s GS1 licence for prefix {prefix}: the certificate GS1 gave them, photographed or as a screenshot. The businesses using it are told and send theirs; two members of staff decide whose it is. Until then nothing changes for anybody.
business.clients.gs1.title: GS1 barcodes on their packages
business.clients.gs1.lede: The barcode on {name}’s packages is theirs, never yours: with their GS1 company prefix here, each package of a load you post for them gets its own SSCC under it. Without one, their labels carry our code alone.
business.clients.gs1.none: No GS1 prefix for {name}: their labels carry our code alone.
business.clients.gs1.prefixHint: As GS1 gave it to {name}: 6 to 12 digits, from their licence.
business.clients.gs1.digitHint: The one {name} sets aside for loads you post, so their own systems never give the same code.
business.gs1.claimLede: Send SeeBuyGet staff your GS1 licence for prefix {prefix}: the certificate GS1 gave you, photographed or as a screenshot. The businesses using it are told and send theirs; two members of staff decide whose it is. Until then nothing changes for anybody.
business.gs1.licenceHint: A photograph or a screenshot, readable: the prefix and your company’s name on it.
business.gs1.licenceReady: Your licence is ready to send.
business.gs1.claimSent: Sent. SeeBuyGet staff decide once the businesses using the prefix have answered.
business.gs1.photoFailed: The picture did not go. Try again.
business.gs1.d.claimantOpen: You said prefix {prefix} is yours. {names} {n, plural, one {uses} other {use}} it, and {n, plural, one {has} other {have}} until {by} to send {n, plural, one {its} other {their}} GS1 licence; then two members of SeeBuyGet staff decide. Nothing changes meanwhile.
business.gs1.d.holderAsk: {claimant} says prefix {prefix}, which you use, is theirs. Send your GS1 licence by {by}: two members of SeeBuyGet staff decide whose it is. Until then nothing changes, and your labels carry on.
business.gs1.d.holderSent: Your licence is with SeeBuyGet staff. {claimant} says prefix {prefix} is theirs; two members of staff decide whose it is.
business.gs1.d.decidedMine: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is yours. Their reason: {reason}
business.gs1.d.decidedNotClaimant: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is not yours to print under. Their reason: {reason}
business.gs1.d.decidedNotHolder: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is {claimant}’s: your labels no longer carry it, and the loads you posted keep the codes they were given. Their reason: {reason}
business.gs1.d.withdrawn: The dispute about prefix {prefix} was taken back. Nothing changed.
business.gs1.d.claimantOpenClient: You said prefix {prefix} is your client {client}’s. {names} {n, plural, one {uses} other {use}} it, and {n, plural, one {has} other {have}} until {by} to send {n, plural, one {its} other {their}} GS1 licence; then two members of SeeBuyGet staff decide. Nothing changes meanwhile.
business.gs1.d.holderAskClient: {claimant} says prefix {prefix}, which you entered for your client {client}, is theirs. Send {client}’s GS1 licence by {by}: two members of SeeBuyGet staff decide whose it is. Until then nothing changes, and their labels carry on.
business.gs1.d.holderSentClient: {client}’s licence is with SeeBuyGet staff. {claimant} says prefix {prefix} is theirs; two members of staff decide whose it is.
business.gs1.d.decidedMineClient: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is your client {client}’s. Their reason: {reason}
business.gs1.d.decidedNotClaimantClient: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is not your client {client}’s to print under. Their reason: {reason}
business.gs1.d.decidedNotHolderClient: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is {claimant}’s: your client {client}’s labels no longer carry it, and the loads you posted for them keep the codes they were given. Their reason: {reason}
business.loads.f.packagesHint: Pallets, cartons or crates: each gets a label.
business.loads.f.packagesHintGs1: Pallets, cartons or crates: each gets a label and its own SSCC.
business.loads.f.packagesHintClient: Pallets, cartons or crates: each gets a label — and its own SSCC under your client’s prefix when their record has one.
business.loads.f.crossing: It crosses a border: customs will read its commercial invoice, which you write on the load once it is posted.
business.papers.title: Papers for the goods
business.papers.labelsCoded: {n, plural, one {# label} other {# labels}}, each with its SSCC beside our code
business.papers.labelsOurs: {n, plural, one {# label} other {# labels}} with our code. Add your GS1 company prefix in Business details for an SSCC on each package.
business.papers.labelsBefore: {n, plural, one {# label} other {# labels}} with our code: this load was posted before your GS1 prefix was set, or for a client.
business.papers.labelsNoCount: 1 label with our code: SSCCs need the number of packages, given when the load is posted.
business.papers.labelsOneOurs: 1 label with our code. Give the number of packages when you post a load, for a label on each.
business.papers.gone: The page could not be opened. Try again.
business.papers.invoiceNeeded: This load crosses a border: the carrier cannot take the goods over until you sign its commercial invoice here, or say your own invoice travels with them.
business.papers.invoiceDomestic: Needed when goods cross a border. This load stays in one country.
business.papers.invoiceWhoReads: The driver carrying the goods reads it from pickup on, to show at the border. Nobody else on the carrier’s side reads it — not their office.
business.papers.invoiceStaysWithYou: It stays with you: on a load in one country no carrier reads it.
business.papers.writeAgain: Write a new one in its place
business.invoice.lede: Your own invoice, as customs reads it. Every value and HS code is yours: SeeBuyGet does not classify goods or suggest a code. Once signed it is not changed; a new one takes its place, and the old one is kept.
business.invoice.reason: Why the goods cross the border
business.invoice.hsHint: Yours or your customs agent’s: 6 to 10 digits.
business.invoice.totals: Total {value} · {kg} kg net, of the load’s {gross} kg
business.invoice.declare: I declare that the information on this invoice is true and correct, and that the contents of this shipment are as stated above.
business.invoice.need.number: Give your own number for this invoice.
business.invoice.need.overweight: The lines weigh more net than the whole load does gross.
business.invoice.need.unitValue: The value of one item, 0 or more.
business.invoice.need.originCountry: Choose where the goods were made.
business.invoice.need.hsCode: An HS code of 6 to 10 digits.
business.papers.invoiceNeededOpen: This load crosses a border: customs will ask for a commercial invoice. Write and sign it here, then print three copies for the pouch on package 1.
business.papers.ownPaperCta: Our own invoice travels with the goods
business.papers.ownPaperSaid: Your own invoice travels with the goods: said by {name} on {day}. The carrier may take them over.
business.papers.ownPaperDone: Said: your own invoice travels with the goods.
business.papers.ownPaperUndone: Taken back: the goods wait for an invoice.
business.parcels.title: Parcels
business.parcels.lede: Send parcels from one shop to another, paid from your parcel balance. The person collecting it shows the code you pass on; nobody sends them a text.
business.parcels.openStep1: Open it once. It is a balance with SeeBuyGet in your country, like a store’s.
business.parcels.openStep2: Top it up by bank or another payment service. A payment counts once the payment provider confirms it.
business.parcels.notYetNext: What you can do now: post a load. A load is paid between you and the carrier, not from a balance with us, so it works here already.
business.parcels.openStep3: Each parcel is paid from it when you send it. Its label prints once paid, and money back goes back into it.
business.parcels.opened: Your parcel account is open. Top it up to send.
business.parcels.viewerNoOpen: Somebody in the business who may change things opens it.
business.parcels.heldBy: Held by {company}. Parcels are paid from it when you send them.
business.parcels.rateCard: Your own rate, agreed with {company}: a contract card — {prices}.
business.parcels.rateDiscount: Your own rate, agreed with {company}: {pct}% off the country’s prices.
business.parcels.rateIdle: It does not apply while the country prices parcels the other way.
business.parcels.waiting: Waiting for {amount} to be paid in, reference {reference}.
business.parcels.waitingPushed: Waiting for {amount}: approve the prompt on the phone (reference {reference}).
business.parcels.terms: Topping up below {above} costs {fee}; above it is free.
business.parcels.topUpPhoneHint: It is sent a prompt to approve. Leave it empty to pay by paybill with a reference.
business.parcels.asked: Asked. The balance grows once the payment is confirmed.
business.parcels.sendHint: Hand it in at a shop — or, where you set one below, have it collected from your place. The receiver collects it at a shop.
business.parcels.viewerNoSend: You can see the parcels but not send one. Ask an owner if you need to.
business.parcels.moveOpen: Hand it in at another shop
business.parcels.movePick: It is {price} where it is booked now. From another shop the price can be different: you see it before anything changes.
business.parcels.moveDearer: From {shop} it costs {now} instead of {was}: {diff} more comes off your balance, which then stands at {after}.
business.parcels.moveCheaper: From {shop} it costs {now} instead of {was}: {diff} comes back to your balance, which then stands at {after}.
business.parcels.moved: {id} is handed in at {shop} now. Print its label again: it names the new shop.
business.parcels.f.shopFull: Full now — no place left for a new parcel
business.parcels.f.receiverHint: The shop hands it to this person, with the code you pass on.
business.parcels.f.fragile: Fragile: only carriers that take fragile goods carry it
business.parcels.f.photoHint: What a damage report is read against. One photo for each parcel.
business.parcels.photoFailed: That photo could not be kept. Take it again.
business.parcels.gap.from: the shop it is handed in at
business.parcels.gap.to: the shop it is collected at
business.parcels.gap.receiver: the phone of who collects it
business.parcels.gap.photo: a photo of what is inside
business.parcels.price: At most {price}. What it costs less comes back to your balance once it is collected.
business.parcels.priceShort: Your balance does not cover it yet: it is made unpaid, and paid once you top up.
business.parcels.sentPaid: {id} is paid. Print its label and hand it in.
business.parcels.sentUnpaid: {id} is made, not paid: top up, then pay for it.
business.parcels.listTitle: {n, plural, one {# parcel sent} other {# parcels sent}}
business.parcels.codeHint: Pass this code to the person collecting it. The shop asks for it before handing it over.
business.parcels.paidNow: {id} is paid. Print its label and hand it in.
business.parcels.offRefund: It has not left the shop: it is withdrawn and {amount} comes back to your balance.
business.parcels.offBringBack: It is at a hub: it comes back to {shop} as a new parcel, for {amount}.
business.parcels.offNo: It cannot be called off now.
business.parcels.f.ownPlaceSub: A driver collects it there, in a bag you close
business.parcels.collectHint: Instead of taking parcels to a shop, a driver can collect them at one of your places — a warehouse, a store. You bag them there by where they go, close each bag with its seal and a photo, and the drivers near are told it is ready.
business.parcels.collectBays: Bags you work on at once
business.parcels.collectBaysHint: How many bags you can fill there at the same time.
business.parcels.collectCorner: Closed bags you can keep in a corner
business.parcels.collectCornerHint: Waiting there for a driver, in any free corner. None: each one stands where you work.
business.parcels.dockCorner: {waiting, plural, one {# closed bag waits} other {# closed bags wait}} there for a driver · your corner holds {corner}.
business.parcels.collectAt: Drivers collect at {place}, in the {zone} area. You work on {bays, plural, one {# bag} other {# bags}} there at once.
business.parcels.dockEmpty: Nothing waits to be bagged here.
business.parcels.dockFor: {n, plural, one {# parcel} other {# parcels}} for {zone}
business.parcels.bagCloseLede: Close bag {code} for the road: its seal’s number if it has one, and a photo of it closed with the seal in view.
business.parcels.offPick: It is at a hub. It can come back to {place}, as a driver’s load.
